clue.text: A very quiet, very big sort of tie is suitable

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size for the very big

indicators.note: a sort of tie is a version of the word tie, its letters arranged differently

explanation.surface: A tie that is very quiet in tone and very large is judged just right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges TIE into ITE, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apposite is fitting or well suited to the occasion.

clue.text: Business may be extra-marital

explanation.surface: A remark that a deal might involve infidelity.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or concern; it is also a romantic liaison, often outside a marriage.

clue.text: Fairies have eatables about eleven

indicators.note: about says the food word is wrapped around the number

parts.note: pies are things to eat
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, also a cricket team

explanation.surface: Fairies have a picnic for a team of eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Pixies are small mischievous sprites of folklore, a kind of fairy.

clue.text: Raised by some sucker at the board meeting?

definitions.text: Raised by some sucker at the board meeting?

parts.words: Raised by some sucker at the board meeting?
parts.note: board is the old word for a dining table, and the sucker is someone noisily slurping their first course

explanation.definitionFit: A rounded spoon is lifted to the mouth by a diner sipping broth at table.

clue.text: Old king confused in the airy obscurities of this Athenian

indicators.note: in says the scrambled king goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
mists are vapours that obscure sight

indicators.note: confused says the king's name is scrambled

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch is lost in the fog surrounding a figure from Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles the nursery-rhyme king's name, and 'in' tucks the result inside the fog. Themistocles was an Athenian statesman and general.
explanation.definitionFit: Themistocles was a statesman of ancient Athens who built its navy before Salamis.

clue.text: Scholar has returned money for meal

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a degree holder, so a scholar

indicators.note: returned says the word for money is read back to front

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money

explanation.surface: An academic gets cash back to pay for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reads the money word backwards; 'meal' is ground cassava flour, not a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassava root is ground into a flour or meal called by this name in the tropics.

clue.text: A swinging, , way-out critic

parts.note: gate was 1930s swing-era slang for a hip jazz musician or fan

explanation.surface: A reviewer who is trendy and unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: James Agate was a leading British drama critic of the 1920s to 1940s.
explanation.definitionFit: James Agate was a famous theatre reviewer for the Sunday Times.

clue.text: To press' one to state conclusion — how like Socrates !

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes
I is the Roman numeral one
Cal, short for California, is a US state, put at the conclusion of the word

explanation.surface: A demand that someone state a conclusion, which is what Socrates would do.
explanation.walkthrough: Socrates was known for feigning ignorance to expose others' errors, a habit called Socratic irony.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates feigned ignorance to draw out his pupils, a stance known as Socratic irony.

clue.text: Foreign title an advantage? No, many give it up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from the bottom, so the whole run is turned around

parts.note: an asset is an advantage or benefit
taken as written
C, a hundred in Roman numerals, stands for many

explanation.surface: A question whether a noble title is worth having, answered that many renounce it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give it up' reverses the whole run ASSET + NO + C, giving C + ON + TESSA.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, a title from abroad.

clue.text: Matches here to stay ?

explanation.surface: A question of whether the games will be held in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporting fixtures are scheduled games; fixtures are also fittings left permanently in a house.

clue.text: Colour of a banger

explanation.surface: Asking what shade a sausage is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' suggests the British slang for a sausage; here it is a loud signal rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Maroon is a brownish crimson; it is also a firework or distress rocket that explodes with a loud bang.

clue.text: New formation to ensure a try ? Wouldn't pay now'

indicators.note: a new formation is a fresh arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rugby coach's new tactics guarantee a score.
explanation.walkthrough: Treasury notes were paper money issued by the British Treasury in 1914-28, no longer legal tender.
explanation.definitionFit: This paper currency of the First World War era has long been withdrawn, so it would not be accepted as payment today.

clue.text: Bits of news in your paper for a change

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of the paper's name are switched around

parts.note: the clue appeared in The Times, so your paper is that newspaper's name

explanation.surface: Snippets of news that appear in the paper you are reading, for variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your paper' is The Times, where the clue was printed; 'for a change' rearranges TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: News items are individual reports or pieces of news.

clue.text: Chosen person

parts.note: a member of the Chosen People, the biblical name for the nation of Jacob's descendants

explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites are called God's chosen people in the Bible, so one of them is a chosen person.

clue.text: Man splits drinks with us-bags of them !

indicators.note: splits says the word man breaks the two drinks apart by sitting between them

parts.note: port and tea are two drinks
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man comes between drinks with friends, carrying lots of luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splits' places the man between the two drinks; 'bags of them' plays on the slang 'bags of', meaning lots.
explanation.definitionFit: A portmanteau is a large travelling bag or case opening into two halves.

clue.text: Stupid if broad-minded type ?

parts.note: broad-minded read literally gives someone with a wide or dense head, and dense means stupid

explanation.definitionFit: A dullard or fool is called a dense-skulled person, someone slow-witted.

clue.text: As an afterthought, changes the books

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
alters means changes

explanation.surface: Someone revises the accounts at the last minute.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalters are books of psalms used in worship.

clue.text: Mishap caused by stress--- - I'd go into that

indicators.note: go into says I'd is placed inside the word for stress

parts.note: an accent is the stress on a syllable
I'd is written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone blames an accident on stress and offers to investigate.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unfortunate mischance.

clue.text: Relative finds Ned conscious after smash

indicators.note: after a smash the letters of the words lie in a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Ned comes round after a car crash and recognises a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A child of one's parent's first cousin is a family member, so a relation.

clue.text: Object-to get East sober

parts.note: to demur is to object
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Someone protests at having to keep a sober eastern neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Demure means modest and reserved in manner, so sober.

clue.text: The man on watch ?

parts.note: the man is a male first name, and the watch is a pocket watch whose chain bears that name

explanation.definitionFit: An albert is a watch chain named after Prince Albert, consort of Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Wreath certainly made with deliberation

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland or wreath of flowers
surely means certainly

explanation.surface: A floral wreath is assembled slowly and carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unhurried and deliberate is done at a relaxed pace.

clue.text: The quality classes

parts.note: the quality is an old term for high society, the gentry and nobility

explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the higher social ranks, the top level of society.

clue.text: Use two joints on Sunday ?

parts.note: the two joints are the knees, bent in church on a Sunday, not two roasts of meat

explanation.definitionFit: To go down on both knees, as worshippers do in church, is to put the knee joints to use.

clue.text: River training round Minehead is free

indicators.note: round says the river and training pieces go around the head of Mine

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
PT is physical training
the head of Mine is its first letter, M

explanation.surface: Training around the Somerset town of Minehead by the river costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Minehead is a seaside town in Somerset, but here it is read as 'Mine-head', the first letter of Mine; 'round' wraps the river and training around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exempt means being free from an obligation or duty.

clue.text: A little bit of an animal — bad clue !

parts.note: a mole is a burrowing animal

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of clue are spoilt and jumbled

explanation.surface: A setter complains that a clue about an animal is poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A molecule is a tiny particle of a substance, so a very small bit.

clue.text: It's a possibility concerning literary composition

indicators.note: a possibility here is one possible arrangement of the letters of the words it's a

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A writer considers what might happen in a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibility' rearranges the letters of IT'S A, one possible ordering of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is a genre of writing that ridicules folly, so a form of literary composition.

clue.text: Exhausted by late round

parts.note: late can mean dead, as in the late king
a policeman's beat is his round

explanation.surface: Worn out by a night-time patrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dead beat means being completely tired out.
